intro: Some people you support are affected by drugs or alcohol, and you may be the first to notice a concern.
points: You never diagnose or treat substance misuse, and must never care for people while affected by drugs or alcohol.
If someone is unresponsive or barely breathing, call 999, place them in the recovery position and never make them sick.
Naloxone can temporarily reverse an opioid overdose, but you must still call 999 as its effect can wear off.
Treat people without judgement; dependence is a health condition, and stigma stops people asking for the help they need.
Report safeguarding concerns promptly, including self-neglect and any risk to a child in a household affected by substance use.
Never encourage someone to stop drinking abruptly; alcohol withdrawal can be dangerous, so help them get specialist support.
